## Other ways people try, and why they fall short

- Instagram on the web. instagram.com has messages and no Reels tab, but it still has the feed and Explore, and notifications are weaker.
- Turning off feed notifications. Settings let you keep only message notifications, which stops the app pulling you in, but once you open it, the feed is still there.
- Deleting Instagram. Removes the feed and your conversations with it, which is why most people reinstall within days.
- A time limit. Screen Time or Digital Wellbeing limits the whole app, so your messages stop with the feed. See how to block Instagram on your phone for the levels of blocking.

## Set Instagram up as a messaging app

Whichever phone you have, a few settings make Instagram feel like a messenger instead of a feed: [...] - Message notifications only. In Instagram's notification settings, keep messages and message requests, and turn off likes, comments, suggestions and live videos. The app stops calling you back for anything but people.
- Open it from the notification. Tapping a message notification takes you to the conversation, not the feed. Reply and close.
- Keep the app off your home screen. On iPhone, put Fluid Friction there instead; on Android, move Instagram into the app drawer.

The aim is that every Instagram session starts with a person and ends when the conversation does. Hard blocks on the whole app tend to fail because they also cut off the messages; more on that in why app blockers don't work.

## What changes after a week [...] ## What changes after a week

People who switch to messages only usually notice that they open Instagram about as often, but for a fraction of the time. Replies stay fast, and the forty minute sessions that used to start with a single message stop happening.

## If it stops working

If the feed appears again on iPhone, check that you opened Instagram through Fluid Friction and not the Instagram app, which has no DMs Only mode. Instagram changes its website from time to time, so keep Fluid Friction updated. On Android, if Reels opens again, check that Feature Blocking for Instagram Reels is still on after any phone update.

# Instagram without the feed: keep only DMs and stories

Last updated September 13, 2026 · Android

## Why people want Instagram without the feed

For many people Instagram is a messaging app with a feed attached: friends reply to stories, groups chat in DMs, events get organised there. The feed, with its suggested posts and mixed-in Reels, is what turns a two-minute reply into forty minutes of scrolling. Removing it keeps what you actually open the app for.

## Two ways to set it up in Feurstagram

### 1. Block the home feed entirely [...] ### 1. Block the home feed entirely

This is the default. The feed request is blocked at the network level, so no posts load and there is nothing to scroll. Stories stay at the top, and the bottom bar takes you to messages, search and your profile. Combined with the Reels and Explore blocks, the app becomes Instagram without the feed and without Reels.

### 2. Keep a Following-only feed

If you still want to see what friends post, leave the home feed unblocked and turn on Following feed only. The feed then shows only accounts you follow, in chronological order, without recommended posts. Unlike Instagram's own Following view, it doesn't reset when the app restarts.
